brief: UBS sales commentary argues a sector-rotation story is turning into a correlation story: indices themselves, not just crowded sectors, have started falling. The author parks fundamentals (Memory down 16% in a day but still up 78% YTD) because positioning now matters more than valuation. Unlike July, long-only accounts have not stepped in to buy; hedge fund flow dominates while LO axes remain pre-existing tickets, so there is no clear buyer and no capitulation signal despite sub-July volume. Rising correlation is making popular hedges (semis vs software, semis vs hyperscalers, AAPL as an anti-AI trade) dangerous, since investors can only sell what they own; the author would buy semis against those hedges rather than call an index low. The move is framed as US-specific, not global, since Hong Kong, China and Europe are higher while the S&P falls, reflecting a reassessment of the US multiple premium amid a potential political/geopolitical shift (the "Trump put" helps rest-of-world via lower oil more than it helps US tech). Oil near $100 and a broken equity/bond hedge (correlation now positive) remain the key cross-asset risks.
